full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Taylor Kitsch, Alexandra Daddario & Christopher Walken Set For True Crime-Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ — AFM International Buyers From 12 Territories Launch Film Distribution Network Lokia On Eve Of AFM Jack Whitehall, Nina Dobrev, Greg Kinnear & Andie MacDowell Set For Rom-Com ‘Honeymooners’; HanWay & CAA Launch For AFM View All November 6, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jack Whitehall, Nina Dobrev, Greg Kinnear & Andie MacDowell Ona Wolff; Emma Beiles Howie; courtesy; Gregg Williams EXCLUSIVE : Jack Whitehall ( Malice ), Nina Dobrev ( The Vampire Diaries ), Oscar nominee Greg Kinnear ( As Good As It Gets ) and Golden Globe nominee Andie MacDowell ( Four Weddings And A Funeral ) are set to star in rom-com Honeymooners . Hanway Films will be launching international sales at the AFM for filmmaker Daryl Wein’s ( Something From Tiffany’s ) feature which is described as “a funny intergenerational story about second chances and finding love where you least expect it”. CAA Media Finance is on board for North American sales. The film is produced under Wein’s Explosive Pictures banner. Related Stories News International Insider: Russell Brand Guilty; AFM Fires Up; Trudie Styler Interview News Letitia Wright To Star In Supernatural Horror 'In Her Shadow' For 'Obsession' Producer & Bankside -- AFM Due to shoot in Italy in the first quarter of 2027, the film’s synopsis reads: “Modern Londoners Freddy (Jack Whitehall) and Cleo (Nina Dobrev) have just secretly divorced, convinced they’re better off as best friends. But their amicable split takes an unexpected turn when Freddy’s parents, Marty (Greg Kinnear) and Julie (Andie MacDowell), and Cleo’s mother, Rose, surprise them with the honeymoon of their dreams in Italy. The catch? The whole family is coming along. As the family descends on an idyllic vineyard outside Rome, long-buried secrets, unexpected attractions, and increasingly tangled loyalties threaten to unravel the entire holiday.” Watch on Deadline Daryl Wein said: “With Honeymooners , I wanted to make a romantic comedy that feels funny, heartfelt, surprising, and deeply human. It’s about the messy, unpredictable nature of love at every age, and the absurd lengths we go to hold onto it, set against the breathtaking backdrop of Italy. My hope is to give audiences a joyful cinematic escape that feels both fresh and timeless.” Gabrielle Stewart, CEO HanWay Films said: “It is hard not to feel seduced by Daryl’s vision for Honeymooners . It combines the wit and charm of some of our beloved British rom-coms with the gloss and unadulterated joy of Hollywood comedies, set in some of the most beautiful locations in Italy. This and the brilliant multigenerational cast makes it a film for absolutely everyone.” Jack Whitehall is represented by CAA and Independent Talent Group; Nina Dobrev is represented by CAA and Lighthouse Management + Media; Greg Kinnear is represented by CAA and Anonymous Content; Andie MacDowell is represented by Gersh and manager Risa Shapiro; Daryl Wein is represented by Dalip Sethi at Rain and Jackoway Austen Tyerman. ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel Gets Greenlight At Netflix Kitsch, Daddario, Walken Set For True-Crime Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ Fox Closes $22B Takeover Of Roku, Creating Massive New Streaming Player Senator’s Letters Preview Dems’ Plans To Probe FCC, Big Tech & More Read More About: Comments

title: International Buyers From 12 Territories Launch Film Distribution Network Lokia On Eve Of AFM
full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Taylor Kitsch, Alexandra Daddario & Christopher Walken Set For True Crime-Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ — AFM International Buyers From 12 Territories Launch Film Distribution Network Lokia On Eve Of AFM Jack Whitehall, Nina Dobrev, Greg Kinnear & Andie MacDowell Set For Rom-Com ‘Honeymooners’; HanWay & CAA Launch For AFM View All November 6, 2026 6:27am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Lokia Lokia EXCLUSIVE : Ahead of the American Film Market, international buyers from 12 territories have teamed up to form a new distribution network called Lokia . The 12 distribution partners comprise Wild Bunch Germany GmbH / Wild Bunch Austria (Germany and Austria); Praesens-Film (Switzerland); PRIS Audiovisuals SA (Portugal); Feelgood Entertainment (Greece); Kazoo Films (UK/Ireland); Noori Pictures (South Korea/ Thailand/Vietnam); Filmhouse (Israel); Blitz Group (Former Yugoslavia); Donart Film (Czech Republic); Mars Production (Turkey); and Horizon Distribution (Global Airlines and Shipping). Related Stories News Jack Whitehall, Nina Dobrev, Greg Kinnear & Andie MacDowell Set For Rom-Com 'Honeymooners'; HanWay & CAA Launch For AFM News International Insider: Russell Brand Guilty; AFM Fires Up; Trudie Styler Interview Incorporated in Luxemboug, the Lokia partners will look to develop and produce content together, pool market intelligence, capitalise on licensing and merchandising opportunities and will soon look to acquire content together. The number of companies in the network could grow in coming months. Watch on Deadline The move is a direct response to consolidation in the market and the challenge posed by the declining international pre-sales model. The companies will continue to acquire content individually for their separate markets and exist as standalone financial entities but the aim is to have larger stakes in IP and to be able to monetise and acquire more aggressively. Multiple projects are in development on the Lokia slate but aren’t ready to be revealed yet. The group isn’t expected to be acquiring as one entity at the AFM but that’s the plan a little further down the road. The Lokia network is the brainchild of Michael Favelle of Australia-based sales agency Odin’s Eye Entertainment and Odin’s Eye Animation, and was co-founded and built with Heiko Nemmert, formerly of German outfit Baby Giant. In addition to the challenge of the pre-sales market, the founders say the network was formed to “provide a solution to the puzzle of IP-derived consumer products for independent animated features.” Favelle explained: “Essentially, without worldwide theatrical guarantees before financing and additional finance to also cover IP extension, licensing campaigns are not realistic. But if there is a system where we co-ordinate both theatrical and licensing partners, offer them investment opportunities in the IP for hedging across territories and rights categories, amongst other synergies we can build a scalable repeatable pipeline, not only for animation but equally for live action.” “I knew we had something that might work when the first distributor I pitched the concept to asked if they could invest,” he continued. Founding partner Yong Ho Lee of South Korean buyer Noori Pictures noted: “It’s no secret that the Korean market has not bounced back after the pandemic. The Lokia partnership gives us greater opportunity to expand our business outside of our traditional home territory. The reality is that we are competing against global giants, and while it’s somewhat of a cliché, together we can be stronger.” Co-founder Nemmert supervised the build of Lokia’s operating system (Lokia OS) and runs the company’s operations and production side. Lokia OS is live and onboarding of distribution and licensing partners is under way. According to the founders, the platform puts the network in one working environment: partners submit projects, distributors return revenue forecasts, and financing and licensing partners see the aggregated picture before capital is committed. “Assets, market intelligence and transparent reporting all run through the same system,” they commented. Nemmert expanded: “Partners are responding to three things: they see projects early, their forecasts and input carry real weight in how a film is financed and produced, and they get a view across the whole network instead of working in isolation. Our system makes that coordination routine. And for our production partners, market validation and transparent feedback add clear value.” Former Marvel executive Russell Brown, Lokia’s Chief Capital and Monetisation Officer, is leading discussions with independent licensing agencies for each territory and is in talks with potential global category partners in toys, video games and publishing. The announcement of licensing partners is anticipated later in Q4, 2026. “The licensing and merchandising industry has never had the opportunity to participate in quality independent IP productions in such an orchestrated fashion, which is why we are seeing such a positive response from the major agents we are signing,” said Brown. Andrew Baker, CEO of Kazoo Films added: “Lokia is an innovative new company, giving distributors early access to projects, enabling us to assess and advise on the development of films, giving them the best commercial advantage. We are thrilled to be the partner for the UK & Ireland and look forward to working closely with Lokia and the other distributors to collectively bring market intelligence to early stage animated movies.” Lokia, which will be exhibiting at the American Film Market at Fairmont Suite 411, has also formed a strategic partnership with Fintage House to oversee reporting and manage collection accounts. Fintage House Co-Chairman Robbert Aarts will join Lokia’s board. It’s not the first grouping of international companies we’ve seen in recent years in response to shifts in the film distribution landscape. The Vuelta distribution group was formed in 2023, in 2024 a group of foreign distributors teamed up to help finance films produced by MadRiver, and producers alliance The Creatives has emerged since then. Lokia’s three principals comprise: Michael Favelle, Chief Creative Officer and President of Distribution who founded Sydney-based production, sales and distribution company Odin’s Eye Entertainment in 2006; Heiko Nemmert, Chief Operating Officer and President of Production, who was previously managing director of Berlin-based Baby Giant; and Russell Brown, Chief Capital and Monetisation Officer, who served as Executive Vice President of Worldwide Licensing, Promotions and Ad Sales at Marvel Enterprises and, from 2012, as President of Consumer Products, Promotions and Ad Sales at Valiant Entertainment. ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel Gets Greenlight At Netflix Fox Closes $22B Takeover Of Roku, Creating Massive New Streaming Player Dobrev Rom-Com; ‘Obsession’ Producer Pic; New Int’l Distributor Network ‘Buena Vista Social Club’ Sets Broadway Closing & West End Date Read More About: Comments

full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart , Jake Kanter November 5, 2026 6:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand Getty Russell Brand has been found guilty of rape. After two days of deliberations, the jury at London’s Southwark Crown Court delivered a verdict on seven sexual offense charges, finding the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. Related Stories News Russell Brand Trial Reveals Worst & Best Of TV Industry That Protected, Then Exposed A Predator News Russell Brand’s Lawyer Rounds On Journalist Who Exposed Brand’s Behavior He was found not guilty on two other counts of rape and one of attempted indecent assault, which was reduced from indecent assault during the trial. Brand firmly denied all the charges, based on allegations made by six women . The charges and verdicts are detailed below. Judge Mr Justice Bennathan told Brand that he would be given a “custodial sentence of some length,” and he was remanded in custody until sentencing on Monday. A rape conviction can carry a sentence of life in prison in the UK. Watch on Deadline The verdicts were read out to silence in the courtroom after the judge told those present not to react to the jury’s decisions. Deadline has been reporting daily from a live video feed of the courtroom since the trial began around a month ago. It was initially anticipated to take at least six weeks but has taken less than four. Within minutes of the verdicts, BBC News reported that Brand was being investigated over further rape allegations made by two women. The Metropolitan Police said its investigation “remains ongoing.” Outside the Courthouse, the detective superintendent in the case, Andy Furphy, said Brand “used his influence, status and fame to exploit and sexually offend against women.” “As his profile grew, so too did his sense of entitlement.,” he added. “I hope this conviction sends a clear message that no one is above the law, no matter how famous or powerful they may be.” Over the past month, the court has heard from all the accusers, who have a lifelong right to anonymity. Deadline can report, however, that three of the complainants that Brand was found guilty of sexually assaulting worked in the TV and radio industry, including former employees of MTV and Channel 4. All accusers came forward after seeing allegations about Brand in a Channel 4 documentary in 2023 and reading about him in The Times. Brand’s defense argued that this documentary “poisoned the well of justice deliberately” and “fundamentally corrupted” his accusers, while having a “truly devastating effect” on Brand’s life. The prosecution said the exposé was not a “magic force” that caused six separate women to “recast” their memories, but that it had caused them to come forward and tell stories about their encounters with Brand that had “haunted them for years.” The allegations stretched from 1999 to 2009, a period that saw Brand go from being an unknown actor to, in his own words, “staggering fame” after he started dating superstar Katy Perry. Charge 1, Complainant 1: Rape Complainant 1 alleged that she was raped by Russell Brand after meeting him on the fringes of the Labour Party Conference in 1999. C1 invited Brand back to her hotel room and alleged that he pushed her onto the bed and raped her. Brand, who was not famous in 1999, argued that the encounter was consensual. Verdict : Not guilty Charge 2, Complainant 2: Attempted Indecent Assault Complainant 2, a former MTV employee, accused Brand of attempting to pull her into a toilet at the network’s London offices in 2001. During the trial, judge Mr Justice Bennathan reduced the charge from indecent assault to attempted indecent assault because there was “insufficient evidence” to support the original count. Brand’s defense was that he did not recall the incident, but denied that he attempted any non-consensual assault. Verdict : Not guilty Charge 3, Complainant 3: Sexual Assault Complainant 3 alleged that Brand “lunged and squeezed” her breasts within minutes of their first meeting in 2004 while attending the birthday party of a TV producer at London’s Nordic Bar. Brand denied sexually assaulting Complainant 3, who worked at MTV at the time. Verdict : Guilty Charge 4, Complainant 3: Rape Complainant 3 alleged that Brand grabbed her arm and dragged her into the toilets of the Nordic Bar. The woman claimed that Brand climbed onto the toilet seat, exposed himself, forced his penis in her mouth, and ejaculated. In his defense, Brand argued that Complainant 3 willingly accompanied him to the toilet, where they had a “kiss and a cuddle.” He denied orally raping the woman. Verdict : Not guilty Charge 5, Complainant 4: Sexual Assault Complainant 4 alleged that she was sexually assaulted by Brand at a radio station in 2004 or 2005. She claimed that Brand “grabbed” her, pushed her up against a wall, and kissed her “sloppily and aggressively.” Brand denied the incident. Verdict : Guilty Charge 6, Complainant 5: Rape Complainant 5 alleged that she was anally raped by Brand at his London home in 2009 days after meeting him backstage at his stand-up show, where she gave him consensual oral sex. Complainant 5 said they had consensual vaginal sex at his home,efore alleging that Brand turned her on all fours and unexpectedly penetrated her anally, removing his condom. Brand said the anal intercourse was consensual. Verdict : Guilty Charge 7, Complainant 6: Sexual Assault A former Channel 4 employee, Complainant 6 alleged that Brand demanded a massage and put his head into the area of her genitals during a workplace incident in 2009. Brand told the court that he could not recall the incident.
